data.reasoning: The disagreement stems from an API failure (HTTP 400) in the first model, which prevented it from reviewing LICENSE and .nvchecker.toml, resulting in an 'inconclusive' verdict. The second model successfully reviewed all files and found them safe. The PKGBUILD uses standard, secure practices with pinned git sources and checksums, and there are no malicious install hooks or scripts.
data.disagreement_analysis: The first model (qwen) experienced API errors when attempting to audit LICENSE and .nvchecker.toml, forcing an inconclusive result. The second model (deepseek) completed the audit successfully and found no issues.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to review LICENSE and .nvchecker.toml due to HTTP 400 API errors.
learnings: Distinguish between tool failures (e.g., API timeouts or 400 errors) and actual security inconclusiveness. Tool failures should not trigger a security inconclusive verdict if the unreviewed files are low-risk or if a retry/fallback is possible.
Implement retry logic or fallback models for transient API errors to prevent unnecessary audit escalations.
